units.zh: 趙光逢，字延吉。
units.en: Zhao Guangfeng, whose style name was Yanji.
units.literal: Zhao Guangfeng, style name Yanji.

units.zh: 曾祖植，嶺南節度使。
units.en: His great-grandfather Zhi had served as military commissioner of Lingnan.
units.literal: His great-grandfather Zhi was Military Commissioner of Lingnan.

units.zh: 祖存約，興元府推官。
units.en: His grandfather Cunyue had been a legal officer in Xingyuan Prefecture.
units.literal: His grandfather Cunyue was a legal officer of Xingyuan Prefecture.

units.zh: 父隱，右僕射。
units.en: His father Yin had risen to the post of right vice director of the Imperial Secretariat.
units.literal: His father Yin was Right Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat.

units.zh: 光逢與弟光裔，皆以文學德行知名。
units.en: Guangfeng and his younger brother Guangyi were both widely known for their scholarship and upright character.
units.literal: Guangfeng and his younger brother Guangyi were both renowned for literary learning and moral conduct.

units.zh: 〈（《舊唐書》：光裔，光啟三年進士擢第，累遷司勳郎中、弘文館學士，改膳部郎中、知制誥。
units.en: (According to the 《Old Book of Tang》: Guangyi passed the jinshi examination in the third year of the Guangqi reign, rose through the posts of director in the Bureau of Merit and academician of the Hongwen Institute, and was later made director of the Bureau of Provisions with charge of drafting imperial edicts.
units.literal: (《Old Book of Tang》 states: Guangyi passed the civil service examination in the third year of Guangqi, was repeatedly promoted to Director of the Bureau of Merit in the Ministry of Personnel and Academician of the Hongwen Institute, and was later changed to Director of the Bureau of Provisions, charged with drafting imperial edicts.)

units.zh: 季述廢立之後，旅遊江表以避患，嶺南劉隱深禮之，奏為副使，因家嶺外。）〉
units.en: After the coup in which Jishu deposed and enthroned emperors, he traveled south of the Yangtze to escape the turmoil. Liu Yin of Lingnan received him with great honor and had him appointed deputy commissioner, and he thereafter settled his family in the far south.)〉
units.literal: After Jishu deposed and enthroned emperors, he traveled in the Jiangnan region to avoid calamity; Liu Yin of Lingnan treated him with deep courtesy, memorialized to appoint him as deputy commissioner, and thus he made his home beyond the mountains.)〉

units.zh: 光逢幼嗜墳典，動守規檢，議者目之為「玉界尺」。
units.en: From childhood Guangfeng was devoted to the classical canon and unfailingly observed propriety in his conduct, so that contemporaries dubbed him the "Jade Measuring Rod."
units.literal: From youth Guangfeng loved the classics of antiquity, and in his conduct he always observed rules and restraint; commentators called him the "Jade Measuring Rod."

units.zh: 僖宗朝，登進士第。
units.en: During the reign of Emperor Xizong he passed the jinshi examination.
units.literal: In the reign of Emperor Xizong he passed the jinshi examination.

units.zh: 逾月，辟度支巡官，曆官台省，內外兩製，俱有能名，轉尚書左丞、翰林承旨。
units.en: A month later he was appointed an inspector in the Revenue Bureau. He served in the central ministries and in both the inner and outer drafting offices, earning a name for competence at each step, until he was promoted to left vice director of the Imperial Secretariat and Hanlin academician-in-attendance.
units.literal: Within a month he was recruited as an inspector of the Revenue Bureau, served in offices of the central ministries, held posts in both inner and outer drafting bureaus, and in all gained a reputation for ability; he was transferred to Left Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat and Hanlin Academician-in-Attendance.

units.zh: 昭宗幸石門，光逢不從，昭宗遣內養戴知權詔赴行在，稱疾解官。
units.en: When Emperor Zhaozong went to Shimen, Guangfeng refused to accompany him. The emperor sent the inner attendant Dai Zhiquan with an edict ordering him to join the traveling court, but Guangfeng pleaded illness and resigned his post.
units.literal: When Emperor Zhaozong visited Shimen, Guangfeng did not follow; Zhaozong sent the inner attendant Dai Zhiquan with an edict summoning him to the traveling court, but he pleaded illness and resigned his office.

units.zh: 駕在華州，拜御史中丞。
units.en: While the court was at Hua Prefecture, he was appointed censor-in-chief.
units.literal: When the imperial carriage was at Hua Prefecture, he was appointed Censor-in-Chief.

units.zh: 時有道士許岩士、瞽者馬道殷出入禁庭，驟至列卿宮相，因此以左道求進者眾，光逢持憲紀治之，皆伏法，自是其徒頗息。
units.en: At that time the Daoist Xu Yanshi and the blind diviner Ma Daoyin moved freely in and out of the inner palace and were suddenly elevated to the highest ministerial ranks. Many others therefore sought advancement through occult practices. Guangfeng enforced the law against them, and all were executed; after that such followers largely disappeared.
units.literal: At the time the Daoist Xu Yanshi and the blind diviner Ma Daoyin came and went within the forbidden precincts and swiftly rose to ranks of chief ministers and palace attendants; because of this many sought advancement through heterodox ways. Guangfeng upheld the law and punished them; all were executed according to law, and from then on such followers largely ceased.

units.zh: 改禮部侍郎、知貢舉。
units.en: He was transferred to vice minister of rites with responsibility for the civil examinations.
units.literal: He was changed to Vice Minister of Rites with charge of the civil examinations.

units.zh: 光化中，王道浸衰，南北司為黨，光逢素惟慎靜，慮禍及己，因掛冠伊洛，屏絕交遊，凡五六年。
units.en: During the Guanghua era the imperial order waned and the northern and southern offices formed rival factions. Guangfeng had always been cautious by nature and, fearing that disaster would overtake him, resigned and withdrew to the Yi-Luo region, cutting off all social ties for five or six years.
units.literal: In the Guanghua era the royal way gradually declined and the northern and southern offices formed factions; Guangfeng had always been cautious and quiet, feared calamity reaching himself, and therefore hung up his official cap in the Yi and Luo region, cutting off social contact, for five or six years in all.

units.zh: 門人柳璨登庸，除吏部侍郎、太常卿。
units.en: When his protégé Liu Can came to power, Guangfeng was appointed vice minister of personnel and director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
units.literal: His student Liu Can rose to power, and Guangfeng was appointed Vice Minister of Personnel and Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

units.zh: 〈（《唐摭言》云：光化二年，趙光逢放柳璨及第，後三年不遷，時璨自內庭大拜，光逢始以左丞征入。）〉
units.en: (According to the 《Miscellaneous Sayings of the Tang》: In the second year of Guanghua, Zhao Guangfeng had passed Liu Can in the examinations, yet for three years received no promotion. Only when Liu Can was elevated from within the inner court was Guangfeng at last recalled as left vice director.)〉
units.literal: (《Miscellaneous Sayings of the Tang》 states: In the second year of Guanghua, Zhao Guangfeng passed Liu Can in the examinations; for three years afterward he received no promotion. When Can was greatly promoted from within the inner court, Guangfeng was only then summoned back as Left Vice Director.)〉

units.zh: 入梁為中書侍郎、平章事，累轉左僕射兼租庸使，上章求退，以太子太保致仕。
units.en: Under the Liang he became vice director of the Secretariat and grand councilor, was later promoted to left vice director while also serving as commissioner of land tax and corvée labor, submitted a memorial asking to retire, and was granted retirement with the title grand guardian of the heir apparent.
units.literal: Entering Liang he became Vice Director of the Secretariat and Grand Councilor, was repeatedly transferred to Left Vice Director and concurrently Commissioner of Land Tax and Corvée Labor, submitted a memorial requesting retirement, and was granted retirement as Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

units.zh: 梁末帝愛其才，征拜司空、平章事。
units.en: The last emperor of Liang admired his talent and recalled him as minister of works and grand councilor.
units.literal: The Last Emperor of Liang admired his talent and summoned him to be Minister of Works and Grand Councilor.

units.zh: 無幾以疾辭，授司徒致仕。
units.en: Before long he resigned on account of illness and was granted retirement with the title minister of education.
units.literal: Before long he resigned on grounds of illness and was granted retirement as Minister of Education.

units.zh: 〈（《唐摭言》云：光逢膺大用，居重地十餘歲，七表乞骸，守司空致仕。
units.en: (According to the 《Miscellaneous Sayings of the Tang》: Guangfeng held high office for more than ten years, submitted seven memorials requesting retirement, and finally retired while retaining the title minister of works.
units.literal: (《Miscellaneous Sayings of the Tang》 states: Guangfeng received great employment, dwelt in weighty posts for more than ten years, submitted seven memorials begging to leave office, and held retirement as Minister of Works.)

units.zh: 居二年，復征拜上相。）〉
units.en: Two years later he was summoned back and again appointed chief minister.)〉
units.literal: After two years in retirement he was again summoned and appointed chief minister.)〉

units.zh: 同光初，弟光允為平章事，時謁問於私第，嘗語及政事，他日，光逢署其戶曰「請不言中書事」，其清淨寡欲端默如此。
units.en: Early in the Tongguang era his younger brother Guangyun became grand councilor and called on him at his private residence, where they once discussed state affairs. On another day Guangfeng wrote on the door: "Please do not discuss Secretariat affairs." Such was his purity, restraint, and silence.
units.literal: At the beginning of Tongguang, his younger brother Guangyun was Grand Councilor; at the time he called on him at his private residence and once spoke of state affairs. Another day Guangfeng wrote on his door, "Please do not speak of Secretariat affairs," so pure, few in desires, and taciturn was he.

units.zh: 嘗有女冠寄黃金一鎰於其室家，時屬亂離，女冠委化於他土。
units.en: A female Daoist priest had once left one yi of gold in his care. In the chaos of the times she died abroad.
units.literal: Once a female Daoist priest entrusted one yi of gold to his household; the times were troubled and the priest passed away in another land.

units.zh: 後二十年，金無所歸，納於河南尹張全義，請付諸宮觀，其舊封尚在。
units.en: Twenty years later, with no heir to claim it, he turned the gold over to Zhang Quanyi, prefect of Henan, asking that it be delivered to the temples; the original seal was still intact.
units.literal: Twenty years later, with no one to whom the gold could return, he presented it to Zhang Quanyi, prefect of Henan, requesting that it be given to the palace temples and monasteries; the original seal was still intact.

units.zh: 兩登廊廟，四退邱園，百行五常，不欺暗室，搢紳咸仰以為名教主。
units.en: He twice entered the highest councils of state and four times retired to private life. In every virtue and moral constant he was upright even when unseen, and the gentry all regarded him as a moral exemplar.
units.literal: Twice he ascended the hall of state, four times he retired to hill and garden, in the hundred conduct and five constants he did not deceive even in a dark room, and the gentry all looked up to him as a teacher of reputation and conduct.

units.zh: 天成初，遷太保致仕，封齊國公，卒於洛陽。
units.en: Early in the Tiancheng era he retired as grand guardian, was enfeoffed as duke of Qi, and died at Luoyang.
units.literal: At the beginning of Tiancheng he was transferred to retirement as Grand Guardian, enfeoffed as Duke of Qi, and died at Luoyang.

units.zh: 詔贈太傅。
units.en: He was posthumously granted the title grand tutor.
units.literal: An edict posthumously granted him Grand Tutor.

units.zh: 光允，光逢之弟也，
units.en: Guangyun was Guangfeng's younger brother.
units.literal: Guangyun was Guangfeng's younger brother.

units.zh: （新舊《唐書》俱云：趙隱子三人，光逢、光裔、光允。
units.en: (Both the Old and New Books of Tang state: Zhao Yin had three sons—Guangfeng, Guangyi, and Guangyun.
units.literal: (Both the Old and New Books of Tang state: Zhao Yin had three sons—Guangfeng, Guangyi, and Guangyun.

units.zh: 為後唐相者，光允也。
units.en: The one who became chief minister under Later Tang was Guangyun.
units.literal: The one who became chief minister under Later Tang was Guangyun.

units.zh: 原本作光裔，係誤。）
units.en: The original text had Guangyi, which was an error.)
units.literal: The original text had Guangyi, which was an error.)

units.zh: 俱以詞藝知名，亦登進士第。
units.en: Both were renowned for literary talent and also passed the jinshi examination.
units.literal: Both were renowned for literary talent and also passed the jinshi examination.

units.zh: （《舊唐書》云：大順二年，進士登第。
units.en: (According to the Old Book of Tang: in the second year of Dashun he passed the jinshi examination.
units.literal: (According to the Old Book of Tang: in the second year of Dashun he passed the jinshi examination.

units.zh: 天祐初，累官至駕部郎中。）
units.en: At the beginning of Tianyou he rose through successive posts to director of the Bureau of Transport.)
units.literal: At the beginning of Tianyou he rose through successive posts to director of the Bureau of Transport.)

units.zh: 光允仕梁，曆清顯，伯仲之間，咸以方雅自高，北人聞其名者，皆望風欽重。
units.en: Guangyun served Liang in prominent offices. Among the brothers each held himself aloof with refined reserve, and northerners who heard their names all revered them from afar.
units.literal: Guangyun served Liang in prominent offices; among the brothers each held himself aloof with refined reserve, and northerners who heard their names all bowed to their reputation from afar.

units.zh: 及莊宗平定汴、洛，時盧程以狂妄免，郭崇韜自勳臣拜，議者以為國朝典禮故實，須訪前代名家，咸曰光允有宰相器。
units.en: When Zhuangzong pacified Bian and Luoyang, Lu Cheng was dismissed for arrogance and Guo Chongyao was appointed from among meritorious ministers. Commentators held that the dynasty's ritual and precedents required consulting celebrated masters of former ages, and all said Guangyun had the makings of a chief minister.
units.literal: When Zhuangzong pacified Bian and Luo, Lu Cheng was dismissed for arrogance and Guo Chongyao was appointed from among meritorious ministers. Commentators held that the dynasty's ritual and precedents required consulting celebrated masters of former ages, and all said Guangyun had the makings of a chief minister.

units.zh: 薛廷珪、李琪當武皇為晉王時，嘗因為冊使至太原，故皆有宿望，當時咸謂宜處台司。
units.en: Xue Tinggui and Li Qi, when the Martial Emperor was Prince of Jin, had once served as investiture envoys to Taiyuan and therefore both enjoyed longstanding reputation; at the time all said they were fit for the highest council posts.
units.literal: Xue Tinggui and Li Qi, when the Martial Emperor was Prince of Jin, had once served as investiture envoys to Taiyuan and therefore both enjoyed longstanding reputation; at the time all said they were fit for the highest council posts.

units.zh: 郭崇韜采言事者雲，廷珪朽老，浮華無相業；
units.en: Guo Chongyao adopted the words of memorialists, saying Tinggui was decrepit and aged, showy without ministerial substance;
units.literal: Guo Chongyao adopted the words of memorialists, saying Tinggui was decrepit and aged, showy without ministerial substance;

units.zh: 琪雖文學高，傾險無士風，皆不可相，乃止。
units.en: and though Qi's literary learning was high, he was treacherous without the bearing of a gentleman—neither could be made chief minister, and the matter was dropped.
units.literal: and though Qi's literary learning was high, he was treacherous without the bearing of a gentleman—neither could be made chief minister, and the matter was dropped.

units.zh: 同光元年十一月，光允與韋說並拜平章事。
units.en: In the eleventh month of the first year of Tongguang, Guangyun and Wei Yue were jointly appointed grand councilors.
units.literal: In the eleventh month of the first year of Tongguang, Guangyun and Wei Yue were jointly appointed grand councilors.

units.zh: 光允生於季末，漸染時風，雖欲躍鱗振翮，仰希前輩，然才力無餘，未能恢遠，朝廷每有禮樂制度、沿革擬議，以為己任；
units.en: Guangyun was born at the close of a dynasty and absorbed the habits of the age. Though he wished to soar like his forebears, his talents fell short and he could not reach their breadth. Whenever the court debated ritual, music, institutions, or reforms, he took such matters upon himself;
units.literal: Guangyun was born at the end of an age and was gradually dyed by the fashions of the time; although he wished to leap like a fish with scales or beat wings like a bird and look up to his predecessors, yet his talent and strength had no surplus and he could not expand far. Whenever the court had matters of ritual, music, institutions, or deliberations on change and continuation, he took them as his own duty;

units.zh: 同列既匪博通，見其浮譚橫議，莫之測也。
units.en: but his colleagues were not deeply learned and, hearing his loose talk and sweeping pronouncements, could not tell whether he truly understood such matters.
units.literal: His colleagues were not broadly learned, and seeing his idle talk and unrestrained discussion, none could fathom him.

units.zh: 豆盧革雖憑門地，在本朝時，仕進尚微，久從使府，朝章典禮，未能深悉。
units.en: Doulu Ge, though he relied on his family's standing, had risen only modestly under the present dynasty and had long served in commissioner offices, so that he did not deeply understand court ritual and precedent.
units.literal: Although Doulu Ge relied on his family standing, in the present dynasty his advancement was still slight; he had long followed commissioner offices and could not deeply understand court regulations and ceremonial rites.

units.zh: 光允每有發論，革但唯唯而已。
units.en: Whenever Guangyun launched into discussion, Ge could only murmur agreement.
units.literal: Whenever Guangyun offered a pronouncement, Ge could only murmur assent.

units.zh: 後革奏議或當，光允謂群官曰：「昨有所議，前座一言粗當，近日差進，學者其可已乎！」
units.en: Later, when Ge's memorial opinions sometimes hit the mark, Guangyun told the assembled officials, "In yesterday's discussion the gentleman in the front row had one remark that was roughly correct. He has improved a little of late—must a student go on forever!"
units.literal: Later when Ge's memorial opinions were sometimes correct, Guangyun said to the assembled officials, "In yesterday's discussion, the gentleman in the front seat had one remark roughly correct; recently he has improved somewhat—can a student not stop here!"

units.zh: 其自負如此。
units.en: Such was the measure of his self-regard.
units.literal: So self-confident was he.

units.zh: 先是，條製：「權豪強買人田宅，或陷害籍沒，顯有屈塞者，許人自理。」
units.en: Earlier a regulation had provided: "When powerful families forcibly bought people's land and houses, or had them framed and their property confiscated, and injustice was plainly evident, the victims might plead their own case."
units.literal: Earlier there was a regulation: "When powerful families forcibly bought people's fields and houses, or framed them for confiscation and registration, and injustice was plainly evident, people were permitted to plead their own case."

units.zh: 內官楊希朗者，故觀軍容使復恭從孫也，援例理復恭舊業。
units.en: The inner attendant Yang Xilang, a collateral descendant of the former army supervisor Fu Gong, cited this precedent to claim Fu Gong's former estates.
units.literal: The inner attendant Yang Xilang was the collateral descendant of the former Army Supervisor Fu Gong, and cited precedent to claim Fu Gong's former estates.

units.zh: 事下中書，光允謂崇韜曰：「復恭與山南謀逆，顯當國法，本朝未經昭雪，安得論理？」
units.en: When the matter reached the Secretariat, Guangyun said to Guo Chongtao, "Fu Gong conspired in rebellion with the Shannan faction and plainly deserved punishment under the law. Our dynasty has not yet cleared his name—how can his estates be claimed?"
units.literal: The matter was sent down to the Secretariat, and Guangyun said to Chongyao, "Fu Gong plotted rebellion with Shannan and clearly deserved the national law; the present dynasty has not yet cleared his name—how can his case be argued?"

units.zh: 崇韜私抑宦者，因具奏聞。
units.en: Chongtao privately blocked the eunuch's claim and submitted a full report to the throne.
units.literal: Chongyao privately restrained the eunuch and therefore submitted a full report to the throne.

units.zh: 希朗泣訴於莊宗，莊宗令自見光允言之。
units.en: Xilang tearfully appealed to Emperor Zhuangzong, who ordered him to go in person and argue the matter before Guangyun.
units.literal: Xilang tearfully appealed to Emperor Zhuangzong, and Zhuangzong ordered him to go in person to speak with Guangyun.

units.zh: 希朗陳訴：「叔祖復光有大功於王室，伯祖復恭為張浚所構，得罪前朝，當時強臣掣肘，國命不行，及王行瑜伏誅，德音昭洗，制書尚在，相公本朝世族，諳練故事，安得謂之未雪耶！
units.en: Xilang argued: "My grand-uncle Fuguang rendered great service to the throne. My elder grand-uncle Fu Gong was framed by Zhang Jun and fell afoul of the former dynasty, when powerful ministers constrained the throne and imperial orders could not be enforced. After Wang Xingyu was executed, an edict of grace publicly cleared the record, and that edict still survives. Your Excellency is a hereditary minister of our dynasty and well versed in precedent—how can you say his name has not been cleared!
units.literal: Xilang stated his appeal: "My grand-uncle Fuguang rendered great merit to the royal house; my elder-uncle Fu Gong was framed by Zhang Jun and offended the former dynasty. At the time powerful ministers checked the throne and the national command did not prevail. When Wang Xingyu was executed, an edict of grace publicly cleared the record and the edict still exists. Your Excellency is a hereditary clan of the present dynasty and well versed in precedent—how can you say his name has not been cleared!

units.zh: 若言未雪，吾伯氏彥博，洎諸昆仲，監護軍鎮，何途得進！」
units.en: If his name were still uncleared, how could my elder clansman Yanbo and all our brothers hold supervisory posts in the military commissions and advance as they have!"
units.literal: If you say his name has not been cleared, how could my elder clansman Yanbo, together with all our brothers, hold supervisory posts in the military commissions and advance by what path!"

units.zh: 漸至聲色俱厲。
units.en: His voice and manner grew increasingly fierce.
units.literal: Gradually his voice and expression both grew fierce.

units.zh: 光允方恃名德，為其所折，悒然不樂。
units.en: Guangyun, who had relied on his reputation for virtue, was overmatched in the exchange and grew dispirited.
units.literal: Guangyun, who had been relying on his reputation and virtue, was refuted by him and was displeased and unhappy.

units.zh: 又以希朗幸臣，慮摭他事危己，心不自安。
units.en: Moreover, because Xilang was a favored attendant, he feared that other charges might be raised against him and could not set his mind at ease.
units.literal: Moreover, because Xilang was a favored attendant, he feared that other matters might be seized to endanger himself and was ill at ease in mind.

units.zh: 三年夏四月，病疽卒。
units.en: In the fourth month of summer in the third year he died of a carbuncle.
units.literal: In the fourth month of summer in the third year he died of carbuncle disease.

units.zh: 贈左僕射。
units.en: He was posthumously granted the title left vice director.
units.literal: He was posthumously granted Left Vice Director.

units.zh: 鄭玨，昭宗朝宰相綮之侄孫。
units.en: Zheng Jue was the grand-nephew of Zheng Qi, a chief minister under Emperor Zhaozong.
units.literal: Zheng Jue was the grand-nephew of the Zhaozong-era chief minister Zheng Qi.

units.zh: 父徽，河南尹張全義判官。
units.en: His father Hui had been a legal officer under Zhang Quanyi, prefect of Henan.
units.literal: His father Hui was a legal officer under Zhang Quanyi, prefect of Henan.

units.zh: 光化中，登進士第，
units.en: During the Guanghua era he passed the jinshi examination,
units.literal: In the Guanghua era he passed the jinshi examination,

units.zh: 〈（《歐陽史》云：玨少依全義居河南，舉進士數不中，全義以玨屬有司，乃得及第。）〉
units.en: (According to the 《Ouyang's History》: Jue in his youth lived under Zhang Quanyi's patronage in Henan. He failed the jinshi examination several times until Quanyi intervened with the authorities, after which he passed.)〉
units.literal: (《Ouyang's History》 states: Jue in youth relied on Quanyi and lived in Henan; he took the jinshi examination several times without passing, and Quanyi recommended Jue to the authorities, whereupon he obtained the degree.)〉

units.zh: 曆弘文館校書、集賢校理、監察御史，入梁為補闕、起居郎，召入翰林，累遷禮部侍郎充職。
units.en: He served as collator in the Hongwen Institute, collator in the Jixian Institute, and investigating censor. Under the Liang he became remonstrance officer and attendant of the imperial diary, was summoned to the Hanlin Academy, and rose to vice minister of rites.
units.literal: He served as collator of the Hongwen Institute, collator of the Jixian Institute, and investigating censor; entering Liang he became Remonstrance Officer and Attendant of the Imperial Diary, was summoned into the Hanlin Academy, and was repeatedly promoted to Vice Minister of Rites with concurrent duties.

units.zh: 玨文章美麗，旨趣雍容，自策名登朝，張全義皆有力焉。
units.en: Jue's prose was elegant and his manner gracious. From the time he entered official life, Zhang Quanyi had advanced his career at every step.
units.literal: Jue's writings were beautiful and his tone dignified and easy; from the time he gained his name and entered court, Zhang Quanyi had exerted force in all matters.

units.zh: 貞明中，拜平章事。
units.en: During the Zhenming era he was appointed grand councilor.
units.literal: In the Zhenming era he was appointed Grand Councilor.

units.zh: 莊宗入汴，責授萊州司戶，未幾，量移曹州司馬。
units.en: When Emperor Zhuangzong took Bian, Jue was demoted to registrar of Lai Prefecture and soon afterward transferred to vice prefect of Cao Prefecture.
units.literal: When Zhuangzong entered Bian, Jue was demoted and appointed Registrar of Lai Prefecture; before long he was transferred by degree to Vice Prefect of Cao Prefecture.

units.zh: 張全義言於郭崇韜，將復相之，尋入為太子賓客。
units.en: Zhang Quanyi spoke to Guo Chongtao about restoring him as chief minister, and he was soon recalled as guest of the heir apparent.
units.literal: Zhang Quanyi spoke to Guo Chongyao about restoring him as chief minister; soon afterward he entered court as Guest of the Heir Apparent.

units.zh: 明宗即位，任圜自蜀至，安重誨不欲圜獨拜宰輔，共議朝望一人共之。
units.en: When Emperor Mingzong took the throne, Ren Yuan arrived from Shu. An Chonghui did not want Yuan to serve as chief minister alone and the court discussed appointing another eminent figure to share the post.
units.literal: When Emperor Mingzong took the throne, Ren Yuan arrived from Shu; An Chonghui did not wish Yuan alone to be appointed chief minister and jointly discussed finding one person of court esteem to share the post.

units.zh: 孔循言玨貞明時久在中書，性畏慎而長者，美詞翰，好人物，重誨即奏與任圜並命為相。
units.en: Kong Xun said that Jue had long served in the Secretariat during the Zhenming era, was cautious and steady by nature, excelled at composition, and delighted in talented men. Chonghui thereupon memorialized to appoint him grand councilor alongside Ren Yuan.
units.literal: Kong Xun said that Jue had long served in the Secretariat during Zhenming, was by nature cautious and elder-like, excelled in literary composition, and loved talented men; Chonghui thereupon memorialized to appoint him together with Ren Yuan as chief ministers.

units.zh: 有頃，玨以老病耳疾，不任中書事，四上章請，明宗惜之，久而方允，乃授開府儀同三司，行尚書左僕射致仕，仍賜鄭州莊一區。
units.en: Before long Jue, citing old age, illness, and deafness, declared himself unfit for Secretariat duties and submitted four memorials asking to retire. Emperor Mingzong was reluctant but eventually consented, granting him the title kaifu yitong sansi and acting left vice director in retirement, together with an estate in Zheng Prefecture.
units.literal: Before long Jue, on grounds of old age, illness, and ear ailment, could not bear Secretariat duties; he submitted four memorials requesting release. Mingzong regretted it and only after a long time granted permission; he was then granted Kaifu Yitong Sansi and Acting Left Vice Director with retirement, and was still bestowed one estate district in Zheng Prefecture.

units.zh: 明宗自汴還洛陽，遣中使撫問，賜錢二十萬，食羊百口。
units.en: When Emperor Mingzong returned from Bian to Luoyang, he sent a palace envoy to inquire after Jue's health and granted him two hundred thousand in cash and a hundred sheep.
units.literal: When Mingzong returned from Bian to Luoyang, he sent a palace envoy to comfort and inquire, granting two hundred thousand in cash and one hundred sheep for food.

units.zh: 長興初卒。
units.en: He died early in the Changxing era.
units.literal: He died at the beginning of the Changxing era.

units.zh: 贈司空。
units.en: He was posthumously granted the title minister of works.
units.literal: He was posthumously granted Minister of Works.

units.zh: 初，玨應進士，十九年方登第，名姓為第十九人，自登第凡十九年為宰相，又昆仲之次第十九，時亦異之。
units.en: When Jue first sat for the jinshi examination, nineteen years passed before he passed, ranking nineteenth on the rolls. Nineteen years after passing he became chief minister, and he was also the nineteenth child among his brothers—contemporaries regarded all this as remarkable.
units.literal: Earlier, when Jue took the jinshi examination, nineteen years passed before he passed; his name ranked nineteenth; from passing the examination it was nineteen years in all before he became chief minister; moreover he was the nineteenth among his brothers in birth order—at the time this was also considered strange.

units.zh: 子遘，太平興國中任正郎。
units.en: His son Gou served as a director of a bureau (zhenglang) during the Taiping Xingguo era.
units.literal: His son You, in the Taiping Xingguo era, served as Regular Gentleman.

units.zh: 崔協，字思化。
units.en: Cui Xie, whose style name was Sihua.
units.literal: Cui Xie, style name Sihua.

units.zh: 遠祖清河太守第二子寅，仕後魏為太子洗馬，因為清河小房，至唐朝盛為流品。
units.en: A remote ancestor, Yin, second son of the prefect of Qinghe, served the Northern Wei as crown prince groom and founded the lesser branch of the Qinghe Cui clan, which by the Tang had become a leading family.
units.literal: A remote ancestor, the second son Yin of the Qinghe prefect, served the Later Wei as Crown Prince Groom and thereby became the lesser branch of Qinghe; by the Tang dynasty this line flourished as a distinguished clan.

units.zh: 曾祖邠，太常卿，祖瓘，吏部尚書。
units.en: His great-grandfather Bin had been director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, and his grandfather Guan minister of personnel.
units.literal: His great-grandfather Bin was Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices; his grandfather Guan was Minister of Personnel.

units.zh: 父彥融，楚州刺史。
units.en: His father Yanrong had been prefect of Chu Prefecture.
units.literal: His father Yanrong was prefect of Chu Prefecture.

units.zh: 彥融素與崔蕘善，嘗為萬年令，蕘謁於縣，彥融未出，見案上有尺題，皆賂遺中貴人，蕘知其由徑，始惡其為人。
units.en: Yanrong had long been friendly with Cui Rao. When Yanrong was magistrate of Wannian County, Rao called at the yamen before Yanrong had come out and saw on the desk a list of names—all gifts to inner attendants. Rao understood his methods and came to despise him.
units.literal: Yanrong had long been on good terms with Cui Rao; he once served as magistrate of Wannian County. Rao called at the county office while Yanrong had not yet come out; he saw on the desk a list of names, all bribes to inner attendants. Rao knew his crooked ways and began to detest his character.

units.zh: 及除司勳郎中，蕘為左丞，通刺不見，蕘謂曰：「郎中行止鄙雜，故未見。」
units.en: When Yanrong was appointed director in the Bureau of Merit, Rao was left vice director. Yanrong sent a visiting card but was refused an audience. Rao said, "The director's conduct is vulgar and corrupt—that is why I will not receive him."
units.literal: When Yanrong was appointed Director in the Bureau of Merit, Rao was Left Vice Director; Yanrong sent a visiting card but was not received. Rao said, "The Director's conduct is base and mixed—therefore I do not see him."

units.zh: 宰相知之，改楚州刺史，卒於任。
units.en: The chief minister learned of the affair and transferred Yanrong to prefect of Chu Prefecture, where he died in office.
units.literal: The chief minister learned of it and transferred him to prefect of Chu Prefecture; he died in office.

units.zh: 誡其子曰：「世世無忘蕘。」
units.en: He admonished his sons: "Never forget Rao, generation after generation."
units.literal: He admonished his sons, saying, "Generation after generation do not forget Rao."

units.zh: 故其子弟常云「崔仇」。
units.en: His descendants therefore often spoke of "the Cui feud."
units.literal: Therefore his sons and younger relatives often spoke of "the Cui feud."

units.zh: 協即彥融之子也。
units.en: Xie was Yanrong's son.
units.literal: Xie was the son of Yanrong.

units.zh: 幼有孝行，登進士第，釋褐為度支巡官、渭南尉，直史館，曆三署，入梁為左司郎中、萬年令、給事中，累官至兵部侍郎。
units.en: He was known from youth for filial devotion. After passing the jinshi examination he began as an inspector in the Revenue Bureau and magistrate of Weinan, served in the Historiography Institute, passed through three central offices, and under the Liang rose through director of the left department, magistrate of Wannian, and supervising secretary to vice minister of war.
units.literal: From youth he had filial conduct; he passed the jinshi examination, took his first office as inspector of the Revenue Bureau and magistrate of Weinan, served directly in the Historiography Institute, passed through three offices, entered Liang as Director of the Left Department, magistrate of Wannian, and Supervising Secretary, and was repeatedly promoted to Vice Minister of War.

units.zh: 與中書舍人崔居儉相遇於幕次，協厲聲而言曰：「崔蕘之子，何敢相見！」
units.en: He encountered the secretariat drafter Cui Jujian in the curtain office and cried out, "Son of Cui Rao—how dare you show your face before me!"
units.literal: He met Secretariat Drafter Cui Jujian in the curtain office, and Xie spoke in a harsh voice, saying, "Son of Cui Rao—how dare you meet my gaze!"

units.zh: 居儉亦報之。
units.en: Jujian retorted in kind.
units.literal: Jujian also retorted to him.

units.zh: 左降太子詹事，俄拜吏部侍郎。
units.en: He was demoted to supervisor of the household of the heir apparent but was soon appointed vice minister of personnel.
units.literal: He was demoted to Supervisor of the Household of the Heir Apparent; before long he was appointed Vice Minister of Personnel.

units.zh: 同光初，改御史中丞，憲司舉奏，多以文字錯誤，屢受責罰。
units.en: Early in the Tongguang era he became censor-in-chief, but the memorials submitted by his office often contained textual errors, and he was repeatedly reprimanded.
units.literal: At the beginning of Tongguang he was changed to Censor-in-Chief; when the censorate submitted impeachments, many had errors in wording and he repeatedly received reprimands and punishments.

units.zh: 協器宇宏爽，高談虛論，多不近理，時人以為虛有其表。
units.en: Xie had a grand manner and loved lofty discourse, but much of what he said was empty and unreasonable, and contemporaries regarded him as all show.
units.literal: Xie's bearing was broad and open; he engaged in lofty talk and empty discourse that often did not approach reason, and people of the time thought he had only the appearance without the substance.

units.zh: 天成初，遷禮部尚書、太常卿，因樞密使孔循保薦，拜平章事。
units.en: Early in the Tiancheng era he was made minister of rites and director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, and on the recommendation of privy council commissioner Kong Xun was appointed grand councilor.
units.literal: At the beginning of Tiancheng he was transferred to Minister of Rites and Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices; through the recommendation of Privy Council Commissioner Kong Xun he was appointed Grand Councilor.

units.zh: 初，豆盧革、韋說得罪，執政議命相，樞密使孔循意不欲河朔人居相位，任圜欲相李琪，而鄭玨素與琪不協，孔循亦惡琪，謂安重誨曰：「李琪非無藝學，但不廉耳。
units.en: When Doulu Ge and Wei Yue fell from power, the court debated a new chief minister. Kong Xun did not want a man from the region north of the Yellow River in the post. Ren Yuan favored Li Qi, but Zheng Jue had long been at odds with Qi and Kong Xun also disliked him. Kong told An Chonghui, "Li Qi is learned enough, but he is not honest.
units.literal: Earlier, when Doulu Ge and Wei Yue offended and were punished, the administration discussed appointing a chief minister. Privy Council Commissioner Kong Xun's intent was not to let a man of the Hebei-Shandong region hold the chief minister's seat; Ren Yuan wished to make Li Qi chief minister, but Zheng Jue had long been at odds with Qi, and Kong Xun also detested Qi. He said to An Chonghui, "Li Qi is not without learning and skill, but he is not incorrupt.

units.zh: 朝論莫若崔協。」
units.en: In the court's view none was better than Cui Xie."
units.literal: In court discussion none was better than Cui Xie."

units.zh: 重誨然之，因奏擇相。
units.en: Chonghui agreed and memorialized to select a chief minister.
units.literal: Chonghui approved and therefore memorialized to select a chief minister.

units.zh: 明宗曰：「誰可？」
units.en: Emperor Mingzong asked, "Who is suitable?"
units.literal: Mingzong said, "Who is suitable?"

units.zh: 乃以協對。
units.en: They named Xie.
units.literal: They answered with Xie.

units.zh: 任圜奏曰：「重誨被人欺賣，如崔協者，少識文字，時人謂之『沒字碑』。
units.en: Ren Yuan objected: "Chonghui is being duped. A man like Cui Xie can barely read—people call him the 'Stele Without Characters.'
units.literal: Ren Yuan memorialized, saying, "Chonghui has been deceived and sold off. A man like Cui Xie scarcely knows written characters; people of the time call him the 'Stele Without Characters.

units.zh: 臣比不知書，無才而進，已為天下笑，何容中書之內，更有笑端！」
units.en: I myself am barely literate and advanced without real talent—I am already the laughingstock of the empire. How can the Secretariat hold yet another joke!"
units.literal: Your subject, compared with him, does not know books and advanced without talent—already the laughingstock of the realm; how can the Secretariat contain yet another source of laughter!"

units.zh: 明宗曰：「易州刺史韋肅，人言名家，待我嘗厚，置於此位何如？
units.en: Emperor Mingzong said, "Wei Su of Yi Prefecture is said to come from a great family and once treated me generously—what if we put him in this post?
units.literal: Mingzong said, "Wei Su, prefect of Yi Prefecture—people say he is of a famous house and once treated me generously—how about placing him in this post?

units.zh: 肅苟未可，則馮書記是先朝判官，稱為長者，與物無競，可以相矣。」
units.en: If Su will not do, then Secretary Feng was a judge under the former emperor, is called a steady elder, and never quarrels with anyone—he could serve as chief minister."
units.literal: If Su is still not acceptable, then Secretary Feng was a judge of the former dynasty, is called an elder, and does not compete with others—he can be chief minister."

units.zh: 道嘗為莊宗霸府書記，故明宗呼之。
units.en: Feng Dao had once been secretary in Zhuangzong's chief commandery, which is why Emperor Mingzong addressed him as "Secretary."
units.literal: Dao had once been secretary in Zhuangzong's chief commandery, and therefore Mingzong addressed him thus.

units.zh: 朝退，宰臣樞密使休於中興殿之廡下，孔循拂衣而去，曰：「天下事一則任圜，二則任圜，崔協暴死則已，不死會居此位。」
units.en: After court the chief ministers and privy commissioners rested in the corridor of the Zhongxing Hall. Kong Xun brushed his robes and left, saying, "The affairs of the realm: first Ren Yuan, second Ren Yuan. If Cui Xie dies suddenly, so be it; if he does not, he will end up in this post."
units.literal: After court was dismissed, the chief ministers and privy commissioners rested in the corridor of the Zhongxing Hall. Kong Xun brushed his robes and departed, saying, "The affairs of the realm: first Ren Yuan, second Ren Yuan—if Cui Xie dies suddenly, well and good; if he does not die, he will surely hold this post."

units.zh: 重誨私謂圜曰：「今相位缺人，協且可乎？」
units.en: Chonghui privately asked Yuan, "The chief minister's seat is vacant—would Xie do for now?"
units.literal: Chonghui privately said to Yuan, "The chief minister's seat now lacks a man—would Xie do for the time being?"

units.zh: 圜曰：「朝廷有李琪者，學際天人，奕葉軒冕，論才校藝，可敵時輩百人。
units.en: Yuan replied, "The court has Li Qi, whose learning spans heaven and man and whose family has worn high office for generations. Measured against any contemporary, he could match a hundred men.
units.literal: Yuan said, "In the court there is Li Qi, whose learning reaches heaven and man, whose generations have worn high caps and robes; in comparing talent and testing skill, he could match a hundred men of the age.

units.zh: 而讒夫巧沮，忌害其能，必舍琪而相協，如棄蘇合之丸，取蛣蜣之轉也。」
units.en: Yet slanderers obstruct him out of envy. To pass over Qi and appoint Xie would be like throwing away a ball of storax and choosing instead a ball rolled by a dung beetle."
units.literal: Yet slanderers cleverly obstruct and envy and harm his ability; if you must abandon Qi and make Xie chief minister, it is like discarding a ball of storax and taking instead the rolled ball of a dung beetle."

units.zh: 重誨笑而止。
units.en: Chonghui laughed and said no more.
units.literal: Chonghui laughed and stopped.

units.zh: 然重誨與循同職，循日言琪之短、協之長，故重誨竟從之。
units.en: Yet Chonghui and Kong Xun shared the same office, and Xun daily spoke of Qi's faults and Xie's virtues, so in the end Chonghui went along with him.
units.literal: Yet Chonghui and Xun held the same office, and Xun daily spoke of Qi's shortcomings and Xie's strengths, so in the end Chonghui followed him.

units.zh: 而協登庸之後，廟堂代筆，假手於人。
units.en: After Xie took high office, court documents were drafted for him by others.
units.literal: Yet after Xie rose to office, the court hall wrote on his behalf, borrowing others' hands.

units.zh: 朝廷以國庠事重，命協兼判祭酒事，協上奏每歲補監生二百為定，物議非之。
units.en: Because the affairs of the national academy were deemed weighty, the court ordered Xie to serve concurrently as director of the Imperial Academy. He memorialized that two hundred new academy students should be admitted each year as a fixed quota, and public opinion condemned the proposal.
units.literal: The court, considering national academy affairs weighty, ordered Xie additionally to adjudicate the Director of the National University; Xie memorialized that each year supplementing two hundred National University students be fixed as standard, and public opinion criticized this.

units.zh: 〈（《北夢瑣言》：明宗問宰相馮道：「盧質近日吃酒否？」
units.en: (According to the 《Miscellaneous Notes from Northern Dreams》: Emperor Mingzong asked Chief Minister Feng Dao, "Has Lu Zhi been drinking lately?"
units.literal: (《Miscellaneous Notes from Northern Dreams》 states: Mingzong asked chief minister Feng Dao: "Has Lu Zhi been drinking wine lately?"

units.zh: 對曰：「質曾到臣居，亦飲數爵，臣勸不令過度，事亦如酒，過則患生。」
units.en: Feng replied, "Zhi once visited my home and drank several cups. I urged him not to go too far. Affairs are like wine: excess breeds trouble."
units.literal: He replied: "Zhi once came to your subject's residence and also drank several cups. Your subject urged him not to exceed moderation; affairs are also like wine—when excessive, calamity arises."

units.zh: 崔協強言於坐曰：「 臣聞『食醫心鏡』，酒極好，不加藥餌，足以安心神。」
units.en: Cui Xie spoke up forcefully at the table: "I have read the 'Food Medicine Heart Mirror'—wine is excellent. Taken without medicines, it is enough to settle the heart and spirit."
units.literal: Cui Xie forcefully spoke at the gathering, saying: "Your subject has heard 'Food Medicine Heart Mirror'—wine is extremely good; without adding medicines, it is sufficient to calm the heart and spirit."

units.zh: 左右見其膚淺，不覺哂之。）〉
units.en: Those present, finding him shallow, could not help but smirk.)〉
units.literal: Those nearby, seeing his shallowness, could not help but sneer at him.)〉

units.zh: 四年春，駕自夷門還京，從至須水驛，中風暴卒。
units.en: In the spring of the fourth year, as the emperor returned from Yimen to the capital, Xie accompanied him as far as Xushui Post Station, where he suddenly died of a stroke.
units.literal: In the spring of the fourth year, the imperial carriage returned from Yimen to the capital; he followed as far as Xushui Post Station and suddenly died of a stroke.

units.zh: 詔贈尚書左僕射，諡曰恭靖。
units.en: An edict posthumously conferred on him the title of left vice director of the Imperial Secretariat, with the posthumous name Gongjing, Reverent and Tranquil.
units.literal: An edict posthumously conferred Left Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat; posthumous title Gongjing.

units.zh: 子頎、頌、壽貞，惟頌仕皇朝，官至左諫議大夫，終於鄜州行軍司馬。
units.en: He had three sons—Ji, Song, and Shouzhen. Only Song served the present dynasty, rising to left remonstrating censor-in-chief and ending his career as acting military commissioner of Fu Prefecture.
units.literal: His sons Ji, Song, and Shouzhen—only Song served the present dynasty, reaching Left Remonstrating Censor-in-Chief, and ending as Acting Military Commissioner of Fu Prefecture.

units.zh: 李琪，字台秀。
units.en: Li Qi, whose style name was Taixiu.
units.literal: Li Qi, style name Taixiu.

units.zh: 五代祖憕，天寶末，禮部尚書、東部留守。
units.en: His fifth-generation ancestor Cheng, at the end of the Tianbao era, served as minister of rites and stay-behind regent of the Eastern Capital.
units.literal: His fifth-generation ancestor Cheng, at the end of Tianbao, was Minister of Rites and Stay-behind Regent of the Eastern Capital.

units.zh: 安祿山陷東都，遇害，累贈太尉，諡曰忠懿。
units.en: When An Lushan seized the Eastern Capital, he was killed in the upheaval. He was posthumously promoted to grand marshal, with the posthumous name Zhongyi, Loyal and Virtuous.
units.literal: When An Lushan seized the Eastern Capital, he was killed; posthumously conferred repeatedly to Grand Marshal, posthumous title Zhongyi.

units.zh: 憕孫寀，元和朝，位至給事中。
units.en: Cheng's grandson Cai rose during the Yuanhe reign to the post of supervising secretary.
units.literal: Cheng's grandson Cai, in the Yuanhe reign, reached the post of Supervising Secretary.

units.zh: 寀子敬方，文宗朝，諫議大夫。
units.en: Cai's son Jingfang served as remonstrating censor under Emperor Wenzong.
units.literal: Cai's son Jingfang, in Wenzong's reign, was Remonstrating Censor.

units.zh: 敬方子縠，廣明中，為晉公王鐸都統判官，以收復功為諫議大夫。
units.en: Jingfang's son Gu, during the Guangming era, served as judge on the military commission staff of Duke of Jin Wang Duo and, for his part in the recovery campaign, was made remonstrating censor.
units.literal: Jingfang's son Gu, in Guangming, served as judge of the military commission under Duke of Jin Wang Duo, and for merits in recovery was made Remonstrating Censor.

units.zh: 琪即縠之子也，年十三，詞賦詩頌，大為王鐸所知，然亦疑其假手。
units.en: Qi was Gu's son. At thirteen his rhapsodies, poems, and eulogies greatly impressed Wang Duo, though Duo also suspected that someone else was writing them for him.
units.literal: Qi was precisely Gu's son; at age thirteen his rhapsodies, poems, and eulogies were greatly known by Wang Duo, yet he also suspected ghostwriting.

units.zh: 一日，鐸召縠宴於公署，密遣人以《漢祖得三傑賦》題就其第試之，琪援筆立成。
units.en: One day Duo summoned Gu to a banquet at his headquarters and secretly sent someone to Qi's home with the topic 'Rhapsody on the Han Ancestor Obtaining the Three Outstanding Men.' Qi took up his brush and finished the piece on the spot.
units.literal: One day Duo summoned Gu to a banquet at the government office, secretly sent someone with the topic 'Rhapsody on the Han Ancestor Obtaining the Three Outstanding Men' to his residence to test him, and Qi took up the brush and completed it immediately.

units.zh: 賦尾云：「 得士則昌，非賢罔共，龍頭之友斯貴，鼎足之臣可重，宜哉項氏之敗亡，一范增而不能用。」
units.en: The closing lines read: "Win men and the state flourishes; without the worthy none may govern together. A friend at the dragon's head is precious; ministers who form a tripod are weighty. Small wonder the house of Xiang fell—one Fan Zeng, and still he could not use him."
units.literal: The rhapsody's end reads: "Obtain men then prosper; without the worthy none can share governance. The friend at the dragon's head is thus honored; ministers forming a tripod can be valued. Fitting indeed was the Xiang clan's defeat and ruin—one Fan Zeng yet unable to employ."

units.zh: 鐸覽而駭之，曰：「此兒大器也，將擅文價。」
units.en: Duo read it and was astonished. "This boy is destined for greatness," he said. "He will come to set the price of letters."
units.literal: Duo read it and was startled, saying: "This child is great material; he will monopolize literary prestige."

units.zh: 〈（《太平廣記》：琪總角謁鐸。
units.en: (According to the 《Extensive Records of the Taiping Era》: While still a boy, Qi paid a call on Wang Duo.
units.literal: (《Extensive Records of the Taiping Era》: At the age of hair-ties Qi paid a call on Duo.

units.zh: 鐸顧曰：「適蜀中詔到，用夏州拓跋思恭為收復都統，可作一詩否？」
units.en: Duo turned and said, "An edict has just arrived from Shu appointing Tuoba Sigong of Xia Prefecture recovery grand marshal. Can you compose a poem?"
units.literal: Duo glanced and said: "An edict just arrived from Shu—Tuoba Sigong of Xia Prefecture is appointed Recovery Grand Marshal. Can you compose a poem?"

units.zh: 即秉筆立製，云：「飛騎經巴棧，洪恩及夏台。
units.en: Qi took up his brush at once and wrote: "Flying horsemen cross Ba's plank roads; imperial grace reaches the Xia platform.
units.literal: He immediately took up the brush and composed on the spot, saying: "Flying cavalry pass through Ba's plank roads; imperial grace reaches the Xia platform.

units.zh: 將從天上去，人自日邊來。
units.en: The general will descend from heaven; his men will come from the edge of the sun.
units.literal: The general will go up from heaven; men come from beside the sun.

units.zh: 此處金門遠，何時玉輦回。
units.en: From here the Golden Gate is far—when will the jade carriage return?
units.literal: Here the Golden Gate is far—when will the jade carriage return?

units.zh: 蚤平關右賊，莫待詔書催。」
units.en: Crush the rebels west of the Pass at once; do not wait for the edict to urge you on."
units.literal: Crush the rebels west of the Pass early; do not wait for the edict to urge you."

units.zh: 鐸益奇之，因執琪手曰：「此真鳳手也。」
units.en: Duo was still more amazed and, taking Qi's hand, said, "These are truly the hands of a phoenix."
units.literal: Duo was even more amazed, and grasping Qi's hand said: "These are truly the hands of a phoenix."

units.zh: 時年十四。
units.en: He was fourteen at the time.
units.literal: At that time he was fourteen.

units.zh: 明年，丁母憂，因流寓、齊、魯。
units.en: The next year, after his mother's death, he wandered through Qi and Lu.
units.literal: The next year he entered mourning for his mother, and thus wandered in Liu, Qi, and Lu.

units.zh: 然糠照薪，俾夜作畫，覽書數千卷，間為詩賦。
units.en: He studied by chaff-light and candle-glow, turning night into day, read several thousand volumes, and from time to time composed poems and rhapsodies.
units.literal: Yet with chaff to light firewood, making night into day, he read several thousand volumes, occasionally composing poems and rhapsodies.

units.zh: 唐僖宗再幸梁、洋，竊賦云：「哀痛不下詔，登封誰上書。」）〉
units.en: When Emperor Xizong again visited Liang and Yang, Qi privately composed a couplet: "In grief the throne issues no edict; who will submit the memorial for the feng and shan rites?")〉
units.literal: When Emperor Xizong of Tang again visited Liang and Yang, he privately composed a rhapsody saying: "Grief and pain without issuing an edict—who will submit the memorial for the feng and shan rites?")〉

units.zh: 昭宗時，李谿父子以文學知名。
units.en: During the reign of Emperor Zhaozong, Li Xi and his son were famed for their literary attainments.
units.literal: In Zhaozong's time, Li Xi and his son were renowned for literature.

units.zh: 琪年十八，袖賦一軸謁谿。
units.en: At eighteen Qi carried a scroll of rhapsodies in his sleeve and called on Li Xi.
units.literal: Qi at eighteen, with a scroll of rhapsodies in his sleeve, paid a call on Xi.

units.zh: 谿覽賦驚異，倒屣迎門，出琪《調啞鍾》、《捧日》等賦，謂琪曰：「余嘗患近年文士辭賦，皆數句之後，未見賦題，吾子入句見題，偶屬典麗，籲！
units.en: Xi read the rhapsody with astonishment, turned his shoes around to greet him at the door, and brought out Qi's 'Tuning the Mute Bell,' 'Holding Up the Sun,' and other pieces. He said to Qi, "I have often lamented that in recent years literati rhapsodies wander for several lines before the subject appears. Yours reveals its theme from the opening line, and the diction is classically splendid—marvelous!
units.literal: Xi read the rhapsody with startled wonder, turned his shoes around to welcome him at the gate, produced Qi's 'Tuning the Mute Bell,' 'Holding Up the Sun,' and other rhapsodies, and said to Qi: "I have often lamented that in recent years literati rhapsodies, after several lines one still has not seen the rhapsody's topic. Your lordship from the opening lines reveals the topic, and the pairing is classically splendid—ah!

units.zh: 可畏也。」
units.en: You are formidable indeed."
units.literal: Formidable indeed."

units.zh: 琪由是益知名，舉進士第。
units.en: From that time Qi grew still more famous and passed the jinshi examination.
units.literal: From this Qi became even more renowned and passed the jinshi examination.

units.zh: 天復初，應博學弘詞，居第四等，授武功縣尉，辟轉運巡官，遷左拾遣、殿中侍御史。
units.en: At the beginning of the Tianfu era he entered the Broad Learning and Eminent Rhetoric examination and placed in the fourth rank. He was appointed captain of Wugong County, then recruited as a transport circuit inspector, and later promoted to left remonstrating official and palace remonstrating censor.
units.literal: At the beginning of Tianfu, he responded to the Broad Learning and Eminent Rhetoric examination, placed in the fourth rank, appointed Wei Gong County Captain, recruited as transport circuit inspector, promoted to Left Remonstrating Official and Palace Remonstrating Censor.

units.zh: 自琪為諫官憲職，凡時政有所不便，必封章論列，文章秀麗，覽之者忘倦。
units.en: Once Qi held remonstrating and censorial posts, whenever current policy seemed wrong he submitted sealed memorials setting out his views. His prose was elegant and polished, and readers never tired of it.
units.literal: From the time Qi was remonstrating official and censor, whenever current policy had something inconvenient he necessarily submitted sealed memorials discussing and arraying; his essays were elegant and beautiful—those who read them forgot weariness.

units.zh: 琪兄珽，亦登進士第，才藻富贍，兄弟齊名，而尤為梁祖所知，以珽為崇政學士。
units.en: Qi's elder brother Ting also passed the jinshi examination. Both brothers were equally famed for their literary gifts, but Ting was especially noticed by the Founder of Liang, who made him a Chongzheng academician.
units.literal: Qi's elder brother Ting also passed the jinshi examination; both brothers were equally famous for rich literary talent, yet especially known to Founder of Liang, who made Ting Chongzheng Academician.

units.zh: 琪自左補闕入為翰林學士，
units.en: Qi rose from left supplementing remonstrator to Hanlin academician,
units.literal: Qi from Left Supplementing Remonstrator entered as Hanlin Academician,

units.zh: 〈（《北夢瑣言》：梁李相國琪，唐末以文學策名，仕至御史。
units.en: (According to the 《Miscellaneous Notes from Northern Dreams》: Li Qi, chief minister of Liang, won his name through letters in late Tang and rose to censor.
units.literal: (《Miscellaneous Notes from Northern Dreams》: Liang chief minister Qi, in late Tang rose through literary examination, served until censor.

units.zh: 昭宗播遷，衣冠蕩析，琪藏跡於荊、楚間，自晦其跡，號華原李長官。
units.en: When Emperor Zhaozong was driven into exile and the official class was scattered, Qi hid himself in the Jing and Chu region, kept out of sight, and styled himself Master Li of Huayuan.
units.literal: When Zhaozong wandered in exile, officials scattered; Qi hid his tracks between Jing and Chu, concealed himself, and styled himself Master Li of Huayuan.

units.zh: 其堂兄光符宰宜都，嘗厭薄之。
units.en: His elder cousin Guangfu, who governed Yidu, once treated him with contempt.
units.literal: His first cousin on the father's side Guangfu governed Yidu and once looked down on him with contempt.

units.zh: 琪寂寞，每臨流踞石，摘樹葉而試草制詞，籲嗟怏悵，而投葉水中。
units.en: Lonely and adrift, Qi would sit on stones by the stream, pluck leaves, and draft trial edicts upon them, sighing in frustration before casting the leaves into the water.
units.literal: Qi in loneliness, whenever facing the stream squatting on stones, would pluck tree leaves and try drafting edicts, sighing with resentment and vexation, and cast the leaves into the water.

units.zh: 梁祖受禪，征入，拜翰林學士。）〉
units.en: When the Founder of Liang took the throne, Qi was summoned to court and appointed Hanlin academician.)〉
units.literal: When Founder of Liang received the abdication, he was summoned in and appointed Hanlin Academician.)〉

units.zh: 累遷戶部侍郎、翰林承旨。
units.en: He was promoted in succession to vice minister of revenue and Hanlin academician-in-attendance.
units.literal: Repeatedly promoted to Vice Minister of Revenue and Hanlin Academician-in-Attendance.

units.zh: 梁祖西抗邠、岐，北攻澤、潞，出師燕、趙，經略四方，暫無寧歲，而琪以學士居帳中，專掌文翰，下筆稱旨，寵遇逾倫。
units.en: The Founder of Liang fought west against Bin and Qi, north against Ze and Lu, and sent armies into Yan and Zhao, campaigning on every front with scarcely a year of peace. Qi lived in the command tent as an academician, handling all literary work. Whatever he wrote pleased the emperor, and his favor exceeded that of all others.
units.literal: Founder of Liang fought west against Bin and Qi, north attacked Ze and Lu, sent armies to Yan and Zhao, managed the four directions—momentarily no peaceful year—while Qi as academician dwelt in the tent, exclusively handling literary drafts; his writing matched intent, favor exceeding all ranks.

units.zh: 是時，琪之名播於海內。
units.en: At that time Qi's name was known throughout the empire.
units.literal: At this time Qi's name spread throughout the realm.

units.zh: 琪重然諾，憐才獎善，家門雍睦。
units.en: Qi kept his word, cherished talent, rewarded virtue, and maintained a harmonious household.
units.literal: Qi greatly valued promises, pitied talent and rewarded goodness; his family gate was harmonious.

units.zh: 貞明、龍德中，曆兵、禮、吏侍郎，受命與馮錫嘉、張充、郗殷象同撰《梁太祖實錄》三十卷，遷御史中丞，累擢尚書左丞、中書門下平章事。
units.en: During the Zhenming and Longde eras he served in succession as vice minister of war, rites, and personnel. He was ordered, together with Feng Xijia, Zhang Chong, and Xi Yinxiang, to compile the thirty-volume 《Veritable Records of Emperor Taizu of Liang》. He was promoted to censor-in-chief and then repeatedly advanced to left vice director of the Imperial Secretariat and grand councilor of the Secretariat and Chancellery.
units.literal: In Zhenming and Longde, successively vice minister of War, Rites, and Personnel; ordered with Feng Xijia, Zhang Chong, and Xi Yinxiang jointly to compile 《Veritable Records of Emperor Taizu of Liang》 thirty volumes; promoted to Censor-in-Chief, repeatedly raised to Left Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat and Grand Councilor of the Secretariat and Chancellery.

units.zh: 時琪與蕭頃同為宰相，頃性畏慎深密，琪倜儻負氣，不拘小節，中書奏覆，多行其志，而頃專掎摭其咎。
units.en: At that time Qi and Xiao Qing served together as chief ministers. Qing was timid, cautious, and secretive; Qi was bold, proud, and careless of small proprieties. Most Secretariat reviews followed Qi's wishes, while Qing constantly picked at his faults and reported them.
units.literal: At the time Qi and Xiao Qing were both chief ministers; Qing's nature was fearful, cautious, and deeply secretive, Qi was unrestrained and proud, not bound by small details—Secretariat memorial reviews mostly followed his intent, while Qing devoted himself to picking out and reporting his faults.

units.zh: 會琪除吏是試攝名銜，改「攝」為「守」，為頃所奏，梁帝大怒，將投諸荒裔，而為趙岩輩所援，罷相，為太子少保。
units.en: Once, while Qi was issuing an appointment with a probationary title, he changed the designation from 'acting' to 'holding the post.' Qing reported this, and the Liang emperor was furious and was about to banish him to the remote frontier. Zhao Yan and others intervened on his behalf. He was removed as chief minister and made crown prince junior tutor.
units.literal: When Qi was handling Minister of Personnel examination matters with provisional title, he changed 'provisional' to 'acting'; reported by Qing, Liang Emperor greatly angry, about to banish to remote frontier, but rescued by Zhao Yan and others—dismissed from chancellor, made Crown Prince Junior Tutor.

units.zh: 莊宗入汴，素聞琪名，累欲大任。
units.en: When Zhuangzong entered Bian, he had long heard of Qi's reputation and repeatedly wished to give him a great appointment.
units.literal: When Zhuangzong entered Bian, having long heard Qi's name, repeatedly wanted to give him great appointment.

units.zh: 同光初，曆太常卿、吏部尚書。
units.en: At the beginning of the Tongguang era he served in succession as minister of ceremonies and minister of personnel.
units.literal: At the beginning of Tongguang, successively Minister of Ceremonies and Minister of Personnel.

units.zh: 三年秋，天下大水，國計不充，莊宗詔百僚許上封事，陳經國之要。
units.en: In the autumn of the third year floods ravaged the empire and state revenues ran short. Zhuangzong issued an edict allowing all officials to submit sealed memorials setting forth the essentials of governing the realm.
units.literal: In the autumn of the third year, great flooding throughout the realm, state revenues insufficient; Zhuangzong issued an edict all officials permitted to submit sealed memorials, stating essentials of governing the state.

units.zh: 琪因上疏曰：
units.en: Qi thereupon submitted a memorial, saying:
units.literal: Qi thereby submitted a memorial, saying:

units.zh: 臣聞王者富有兆民，深居九重，所重患者，百姓凋耗而不知，四海困窮而莫救，下情不得上達，群臣不敢指言。
units.en: Your subject has heard that a ruler who possesses the myriad people, dwelling deep within the ninefold palace, should dread above all that the people waste away while he remains unaware, that the four seas fall into destitution while no one can save them, that the grievances below never reach the throne, and that his ministers dare not speak plainly.
units.literal: Your subject has heard that the king who possesses the myriad people, dwelling deep within the ninefold palace, what he most dreads as harm is: the common people wither in decline yet he does not know; the four seas are trapped in poverty yet none can rescue; lower sentiments cannot reach above; ministers dare not point and speak.

units.zh: 今陛下以水潦之災，軍食乏闕，焦勞罪己，迫切疚懷，避正殿以責躬，訪多士而求理，則何思而不獲，何議而不臧？
units.en: Now Your Majesty, faced with flood and military shortages, toils in self-reproach with an urgent and troubled heart, has left the main hall to accept blame and sought out learned men for counsel. Under such conditions, what counsel could fail to be heard, what proposal could fail to be sound?
units.literal: Now Your Majesty, because of flood disaster, military provisions lacking, anxiously toils blaming yourself, urgently troubled in conscience, avoiding the main hall to blame yourself, visiting many scholars to seek order—then what thought would not be obtained, what deliberation would not be good?

units.zh: 止在改而行之，足以擇其善者。
units.en: What remains is to reform and act—enough to choose what is good and put it into practice.
units.literal: It only lies in changing and carrying it out—sufficient to choose the good ones.

units.zh: 臣聞古人有言曰：穀者，人之司命也；
units.en: Your subject has heard the ancients say: grain is the arbiter of human life;
units.literal: Your subject has heard the ancients had a saying: grain is the arbiter of human destiny;

units.zh: 地者，穀之所生也；
units.en: land is where grain is produced;
units.literal: land is where grain is born;

units.zh: 人者，君之所理也。
units.en: and people are what the ruler must govern.
units.literal: people are what the ruler governs.

units.zh: 有其穀則國力備，定其地則人食足，察其人則徭役均，知此三者，為國之急務也。
units.en: With grain the state's strength is secure; with land fixed the people's food is sufficient; with the people rightly assessed corvée and taxes are fair. To know these three things is the urgent business of governing the state.
units.literal: Having grain then national strength is complete; fixing land then people's food is sufficient; examining people then corvée and taxes are equal—knowing these three things is the urgent task of governing the state.

units.zh: 軒黃已前，不可詳記。
units.en: Before the eras of Xuanyuan and Huangdi the record cannot be traced in detail.
units.literal: Before Xuanyuan and Huangdi, cannot be recorded in detail.

units.zh: 自堯湮洪水，禹作司空，於時辨九等之田，收什一之稅，其時戶一千三百餘萬，定墾地約九百二十萬頃，最為太平之盛。
units.en: From the time Yao controlled the great flood and Yu became minister of works, the fields were graded in nine classes and a tithe was collected. Household registers then numbered more than thirteen million, and reclaimed land was fixed at about nine million two hundred thousand qing—the greatest flourishing of the age of peace.
units.literal: From when Yao submerged the great flood and Yu became Minister of Works, at that time distinguishing nine grades of fields and collecting one-tenth tax—at that time households more than thirteen million, fixed reclaimed land about nine million two hundred thousand qing—most flourishing era of great peace.

units.zh: 及商革夏命，重立田製，每私田十畝，種公田一畝，水旱同之，亦什一之義也。
units.en: When Shang replaced the Xia mandate it re-established the field system: for every ten mu of private land one mu of public land was planted, with flood and drought treated alike—the same principle of the tithe.
units.literal: When Shang replaced Xia's mandate, re-established field system: every ten mu of private field, plant one mu public field; flood and drought treated the same—also the meaning of one-tenth.

units.zh: 洎乎周室，立井田之法，大約百里之國，提封萬井，出車百乘，戎馬四百匹。
units.en: By the Zhou dynasty the well-field system had been established. A state of roughly a hundred li enclosed ten thousand wells, furnished a hundred chariots, and four hundred war horses.
units.literal: Down to the Zhou house, established well-field method—approximately a state of a hundred li, with enclosed territory of ten thousand wells, outputting a hundred chariots, four hundred war horses.

units.zh: 畿內兵車萬乘，馬四萬匹，以田法論之，亦什一之制也。
units.en: Within the royal domain there were ten thousand chariots and forty thousand horses. Judged by the field system, this too was a tithe arrangement.
units.literal: Within the capital domains ten thousand chariots, forty thousand horses—speaking by field law, also the one-tenth system.

units.zh: 故當成、康之世，比堯、舜之朝，戶口更增二十餘萬，非他術也，蓋三代以前，皆量入以為出，計農以立軍，雖逢水旱之災，而有凶荒之備。
units.en: Thus in the age of Kings Cheng and Kang, compared with the reigns of Yao and Shun, registered households increased by more than two hundred thousand. This was no other art: before the Three Dynasties all states measured receipts to set expenditures and counted farmers to raise armies, so that even when flood or drought struck they still had stores against famine.
units.literal: Therefore in the era of Cheng and Kang, compared with the court of Yao and Shun, registered population further increased by more than two hundred thousand—not other technique; it was that before the Three Dynasties all measured receipts to determine expenditures, counted farmers to establish army—though encountering flood and drought disasters, had preparation against famine.

units.zh: 降及秦、漢，重稅工商，急關市之征，倍舟車之算，人戶既以減耗，古制猶以兼行，按此時戶口，尚有千二百餘萬，墾田亦八百萬頃。
units.en: By Qin and Han times merchants and craftsmen were heavily taxed, market dues were sharply increased, and levies on boats and carts were doubled. Registered households had already declined, yet the ancient system was still partly kept. Even then the population stood at more than twelve million households and reclaimed land at eight million qing.
units.literal: Down to Qin and Han, heavily taxed merchants and craftsmen, urgently levied border market taxes, doubled boat and cart assessments—registered households already reduced in decline, ancient system still concurrently practiced—according to registered population at this time still more than twelve million, reclaimed fields also eight million qing.

units.zh: 至乎三國並興，兩晉之後，則農夫少於軍眾，戰馬多於耕牛，供軍須奪於農糧，秣馬必侵於牛草，於是天下戶口，隻有二百四十餘萬。
units.en: By the rise of the Three Kingdoms and after the Two Jin dynasties, farmers were fewer than soldiers and war horses outnumbered plow oxen. Army provisions had to be taken from farm grain, and horse fodder encroached on cattle feed. The empire's registered households fell to little more than two million four hundred thousand.
units.literal: Down to Three Kingdoms rising together, after Two Jin, then farmers fewer than army multitudes, war horses more than plow oxen—army supplies necessarily taken from farm grain, horse feed must encroach on ox fodder—thus realm registered households only two million four hundred thousand plus.

units.zh: 洎隋文之代，兩漢比隆，及煬帝之年，又三分之一。
units.en: Under Emperor Wen of Sui the population again rivaled the Two Han dynasties, but by the reign of Emperor Yang it had fallen to one-third of that level.
units.literal: Down to Emperor Wen of Sui's era, compared with Two Han still flourishing; by Emperor Yang's years, again one-third.

units.zh: 我唐太宗文皇帝，以四夷初定，百姓未豐，延訪群臣，各陳所見，惟魏徵獨勸文皇力行王道，由是輕徭薄賦，不奪農時，進賢良，悅忠直，天下粟價，鬥直兩錢。
units.en: Our Tang Emperor Taizong, when the four quarters had just been pacified and the people were not yet prosperous, sought the views of his ministers. Wei Zheng alone urged him to practice the kingly way in earnest. Thereafter corvée was lightened and taxes reduced, farming seasons were not disturbed, worthy men were advanced, and loyal counsel was welcomed. Grain throughout the realm sold at two cash per dou.
units.literal: Our Tang Emperor Taizong the Literary Emperor, when the four barbarians were first pacified and common people not yet abundant, extended inquiry to ministers each stating their views—only Wei Zheng alone urged Literary Emperor to vigorously practice kingly Way—thereby light corvée thin taxes, not seizing farming season, advancing worthy and good, delighting in loyalty and uprightness—realm grain price, one dou straight two coins.

units.zh: 自貞觀至於開元，將及一千九百萬戶，五千三百萬口，墾田一千四百萬頃，比之堯、舜，又極增加，是知救人瘼者，以重斂為病源；
units.en: From the Zhenguan era to Kaiyuan the registers approached nineteen million households and fifty-three million persons, with fourteen million qing under cultivation—far beyond even Yao and Shun. This shows that to relieve the people's suffering one must treat heavy taxation as the root of the disease;
units.literal: From Zhenguan until Kaiyuan, nearly nineteen million households, fifty-three million mouths, reclaimed land fourteen million qing—compared with Yao and Shun, again extremely increased—this knows saving people's affliction takes heavy taxation as disease source;

units.zh: 料兵食者，以惠農為軍政。
units.en: and that to supply the army one must make benefiting agriculture the foundation of military policy.
units.literal: Calculating army provisions takes benefiting farming as military governance.

units.zh: 仲尼云：「百姓足，君孰與不足。」
units.en: Confucius said, "When the people have enough, which ruler will not have enough?"
units.literal: Zhongni said: "When the common people are sufficient, which ruler would not be sufficient?"

units.zh: 臣之此言，是魏徵所以勸文皇也，伏惟深留宸鑒。
units.en: What your subject has said is what Wei Zheng used to counsel Emperor Taizong. I respectfully ask Your Majesty to weigh it deeply in your sage judgment.
units.literal: Your subject's these words are what Wei Zheng used to urge Literary Emperor—respectfully may Your Majesty deeply retain imperial examination.

units.zh: 如以六軍方闕，不可輕徭，兩稅之餘，猶須重斂，則但不以折納為事，一切以本色輸官，又不以紐配為名，止以正耗加納，猶應感悅，未至流亡。
units.en: If, because the Six Armies are still short of supplies, corvée cannot be lightened and heavy levies must continue beyond the two-tax system, then at least do not insist on payment in folded goods; let all dues be rendered in kind. Do not impose additional charges under the name of string-matching; limit extra collection to the regular official measure. Even then the people would still feel grateful and would not yet be driven into exile.
units.literal: If because the Six Armies presently lack and cannot lightly reduce corvée, beyond the two taxes still must heavily levy—then simply not take folded collection as affair, entirely use natural-color goods delivered to government; also not take string-matching as name, only take regular official measure plus additional levy—still should feel grateful, not yet reach exile.

units.zh: 況今東作是時，羸牛將駕，數州之地，千里運糧，有此差徭，必妨春種，今秋若無糧草，保以贍軍。
units.en: Moreover, this is the season for spring planting. Emaciated oxen are about to be harnessed, yet grain must be transported a thousand li from several prefectures. Such corvée duties will surely obstruct the spring sowing. If there is no grain or fodder this autumn, how will the army be fed?
units.literal: Moreover now eastern plowing is the season—emaciated oxen about to harness; several prefectures' territory, thousand-li transport grain—with these corvée assignments must obstruct spring planting—if this autumn without grain and fodder, how can army be supported?

units.zh: 臣伏思漢文帝時，欲人務農，乃募人入粟，得拜爵及贖罪，景帝亦如之。
units.en: Your subject respectfully recalls that Emperor Wen of Han, wishing the people to devote themselves to farming, offered to ennoble men who contributed grain and to allow grain contributions to redeem crimes. Emperor Jing did the same.
units.literal: Your subject respectfully considers when Emperor Wen of Han, wishing people to devote to farming, then recruited people to enter grain, could be enfeoffed with noble rank and redeem crimes; Emperor Jing also was so.

units.zh: 後漢安帝時，水旱不足，三公奏請，富人入粟，得關內侯及公卿以下散官。
units.en: In Later Han, during the reign of Emperor An, when flood and drought left stores insufficient, the Three Excellencies memorialized that wealthy men who contributed grain might receive the rank of marquis within the passes or honorary posts of the Three Excellencies and ministers and below.
units.literal: Later Han during Emperor An, flood drought insufficient, Three Excellencies memorialized request—wealthy entering grain could obtain within-the-passes marquis and various officials below Three Excellencies honorary posts.

units.zh: 本朝乾元中，亦曾如此。
units.en: In our dynasty, during the Qianyuan era, the same measure was once adopted.
units.literal: In our dynasty during Qianyuan, also once was so.

units.zh: 今陛下縱不欲入粟授官，願明降製旨下諸道，合差百姓轉倉之處，有能出力運官物到京師，五百石以上，白身授一初任州縣官，有官者依資遷授，欠選者便與放選。
units.en: Even if Your Majesty does not wish to grant office for grain contributions, I ask that you clearly issue an edict to all circuits. Wherever the people are being conscripted to transfer grain, let it be announced that anyone who transports government goods to the capital at his own expense—for five hundred shi or more—a commoner shall receive an initial appointment as a county or prefecture official; an official shall be promoted according to qualification; and one awaiting appointment shall be granted selection at once.
units.literal: Now though Your Majesty may not wish entering grain granting offices, wish clearly to descend edict to all circuits—places where common people are assigned to transfer granaries—if able to exert strength transporting government goods to capital, five hundred shi and above, white-bodied person granted first appointment county-prefecture official; if already has office, according to qualification transferred; those lacking selection then immediately granted selection.

units.zh: 千石以上至萬石，不拘文武，明示賞酬。
units.en: For one thousand shi up to ten thousand shi, without distinction between civil and military ranks, let rewards be clearly specified.
units.literal: One thousand shi and above to ten thousand shi, not bound by civil or military, clearly show reward and remuneration.

units.zh: 免令方春農人流散，斯亦救民轉倉贍軍之一術也。
units.en: This would keep farmers from scattering at the height of spring planting, and it is one way to relieve the people while moving grain and supplying the army.
units.literal: Avoid ordering in spring farming people to scatter and flee—this also is one technique of saving people through transfer granary supporting army.

units.zh: 莊宗深重之，尋命為國計使，垂為輔相，俄遇蕭牆之難而止。
units.en: Zhuangzong thought highly of the memorial and soon appointed Qi national planning commissioner, intending to make him chief minister. Before long, however, palace turmoil intervened and the appointment went no further.
units.literal: Zhuangzong deeply valued it, soon appointed National Planning Commissioner, about to become assistant chief minister, soon encountered turmoil within palace walls and stopped.

units.zh: 及明宗即位，豆盧革、韋說得罪，任圜陳奏，請命琪為相，為孔循、鄭玨排沮，乃相崔協。
units.en: When Emperor Mingzong took the throne, Doulu Ge and Wei Yue were punished. Ren Yuan memorialized requesting that Qi be made chief minister, but Kong Xun and Zheng Jue obstructed the appointment, and Cui Xie was made chief minister instead.
units.literal: When Mingzong took the throne, Doulu Ge and Wei Yue were punished. Ren Yuan memorialized requesting that Qi be made chief minister, but Kong Xun and Zheng Jue obstructed the appointment, and Cui Xie was made chief minister instead.

units.zh: 琪時為御史大夫，安重誨於台門前專殺殿直馬延。
units.en: Qi was then censor-in-chief. An Chonghui summarily executed palace attendant Ma Yan before the Censorate gate.
units.literal: Qi was then censor-in-chief. An Chonghui summarily executed palace attendant Ma Yan before the Censorate gate.

units.zh: 雖曾彈奏，而依違詞旨，不敢正言其罪，以是托疾，三上章請老；
units.en: Although Qi had memorialized in impeachment, his language was evasive and he dared not state the crime plainly. On this account he feigned illness and three times submitted memorials requesting retirement;
units.literal: Although Qi had memorialized in impeachment, his language was evasive and he dared not state the crime plainly. On this account he feigned illness and three times submitted memorials requesting retirement;

units.zh: 朝旨不允，除授尚書左僕射。
units.en: The court did not approve and instead appointed him left vice director of the Department of State Affairs.
units.literal: the court did not approve and appointed him left vice director of the Department of State Affairs.

units.zh: 自是之後，尤為宰執所忌，凡有奏陳，靡不望風橫沮。
units.en: From this time on he was especially resented by the chief ministers; whenever he submitted a memorial it was invariably blocked on sight.
units.literal: From this time on he was especially resented by the chief ministers; whenever he submitted a memorial it was invariably blocked on sight.

units.zh: 天成末，明宗自汴州還洛，琪為東都留司官班首，奏請至偃師奉迎。
units.en: At the end of Tiancheng, when Emperor Mingzong returned from Bian Prefecture to Luoyang, Qi was the senior official of the Eastern Capital retention bureau and memorialized requesting to go as far as Yanshi to welcome him.
units.literal: At the end of Tiancheng, when Mingzong returned from Bian Prefecture to Luoyang, Qi was the senior official of the Eastern Capital retention bureau and memorialized requesting to go as far as Yanshi to welcome him.

units.zh: 時琪奏中有「敗契丹之凶黨，破真定之逆賊」之言，詔曰：「契丹即為凶黨，真定不是逆賊，李琪罰一月俸。」
units.en: At the time Qi's memorial contained the words "defeating the vicious faction of the Khitan and crushing the rebel bandits of Zhending." An edict said: "If the Khitan are a vicious faction, then Zhending are not rebel bandits. Li Qi is fined one month's salary."
units.literal: At the time Qi's memorial contained the words "defeating the vicious faction of the Khitan and crushing the rebel bandits of Zhending." An edict said: "If the Khitan are a vicious faction, then Zhending are not rebel bandits. Li Qi is fined one month's salary."

units.zh: 又嘗秦敕撰《霍彥威神道碑》文。
units.en: He also once, by imperial command, composed the spirit-way stele text for Huo Yanwei.
units.literal: He also once received imperial command to compose the spirit-way stele text for Huo Yanwei.

units.zh: 琪，梁之故相也，敘彥威仕梁曆任，不言其偽。
units.en: Qi, a former chief minister of Liang, described Yanwei's successive offices under Liang without mentioning the illegitimate regime.
units.literal: Qi, a former chief minister of Liang, described Yanwei's successive offices under Liang without mentioning the illegitimate regime.

units.zh: 中書奏曰：「不分真偽，是混功名，望令改撰。」
units.en: The Secretariat memorialized: "Not distinguishing true from false confounds merit and reputation. We ask that he be ordered to rewrite it."
units.literal: The Secretariat memorialized: "Not distinguishing true from false confounds merit and reputation. We ask that he be ordered to rewrite it."

units.zh: 詔從之。
units.en: The edict approved.
units.literal: The edict approved.

units.zh: 多此類也。
units.en: There were many instances of this kind.
units.literal: There were many instances of this kind.

units.zh: 琪雖博學多才，拙於遵養時晦，知時不可為，然猶多岐取進，動而見排，由己不能鎮靜也。
units.en: Though Qi was learned and gifted, he was poor at biding his time and keeping quiet. He knew when the times forbade action, yet still sought advancement by every path he could find; whenever he moved he met obstruction, because he could not keep himself still.
units.literal: Though Qi was broadly learned and many-talented, clumsy at nurturing the times and concealing himself, knew times could not be acted upon, yet still took many paths to advance—acting and being rejected, from himself unable to be calm.

units.zh: 以太子太傅致仕。
