units.en: He retired as crown prince grand tutor.
units.literal: Retired as Crown Prince Grand Tutor.

units.zh: 長興中，卒於福善裏第，時年六十。
units.en: During the Changxing era he died at his home in Fushan Lane, aged sixty.
units.literal: In Changxing, died at Fushan Lane residence, aged sixty.

units.zh: 子貞，官至邑宰。
units.en: His son Zhen rose to the post of district magistrate.
units.literal: Son Zhen, reached office of district magistrate.

units.zh: 琪以在內署時所為製詔，編為十卷，目曰《金門集》，大行於世。
units.en: Qi compiled the edicts and proclamations he had drafted in the inner secretariat into ten volumes under the title 《Golden Gate Collection》, which circulated widely.
units.literal: Qi compiled edicts and proclamations composed while in inner secretariat into ten volumes, titled 《Golden Gate Collection》, widely circulated in the world.

units.zh: 蕭頃，字子澄，京兆萬年人。
units.en: Xiao Qing, whose style name was Zicheng, was a native of Wannian in Jingzhao.
units.literal: Xiao Qing, style name Zicheng, native of Wannian in Jingzhao.

units.zh: 故相仿之孫，京兆尹廩之子。
units.en: He was the grandson of the former chief minister Fang and the son of Lin, governor of Jingzhao.
units.literal: Grandson of former Xiang, son of Jingzhao Governor Lin.

units.zh: 頃聰悟善屬文，昭宗朝擢進士第，曆度支巡官、太常博士、右補闕。
units.en: Qing was quick-witted and skilled at prose. In the reign of Emperor Zhaozong he passed the jinshi examination and served in succession as inspector of the Census Bureau, doctor of the Grand Ceremonies, and right supplementing remonstrator.
units.literal: Qing was intelligent and quick, good at composing prose; in Zhaozong's reign passed jinshi, successively transport circuit inspector, Grand Ceremonies Doctor, Right Supplementing Remonstrator.

units.zh: 時國步艱難，連帥倔強，率多奏請，欲立家廟於本鎮，頃上章論奏，乃止。
units.en: When the fortunes of the state were dire, regional commanders, headstrong and powerful, often memorialized to establish family temples in their own garrisons. Qing submitted a memorial opposing the practice, and the requests ceased.
units.literal: When national fortunes were difficult, military commissioners stubborn, mostly many memorial requests wishing to establish family temple in their home garrison—Qing submitted memorial discussing and memorializing, then stopped.

units.zh: 累遷吏部員外郎。
units.en: He was promoted in succession to vice director in the Ministry of Personnel.
units.literal: Repeatedly promoted to Vice Director of Ministry of Personnel.

units.zh: 先是，張浚自中書出為右僕射，梁祖判官高劭使梁祖蔭求一子出身官，省寺皆稱無例，浚曲為行之，指揮甚急，吏徒惶恐。
units.en: Earlier, when Zhang Jun left the Secretariat to become right vice director, Gao Shao, a judge on the staff of the Founder of Liang, had the Founder's yin request an initial appointment for a son. All the capital ministries and courts said there was no precedent, but Zhang Jun bent the rules to carry it out. His order was extremely urgent, and the clerks were terrified.
units.literal: Previously, Zhang Jun from Secretariat went out as Right Vice Director; Liang Founder's judge Gao Shao had Liang Founder's yin seek one son's initial-office appointment—all provincial ministries said no precedent; Jun bent rules to execute it, order extremely urgent, clerks terrified.

units.zh: 頃判云：「僕射未集郎官，赴省上指揮公事，且非南宮舊儀。」
units.en: Qing wrote in his decision: "The vice director has not assembled the bureau officials, yet goes to the ministry to deliver an ordered matter of public business—this is not the old procedure of the Southern Palace."
units.literal: Qing judged: "Vice Director has not assembled bureau officials, going to ministry to present ordered public affairs—and moreover not southern palace old ceremony."

units.zh: 浚聞之，慚悚致謝，頃由是知名，梁祖亦獎之。
units.en: When Zhang Jun heard of this, he was ashamed and alarmed and offered his thanks. Qing thereby gained a reputation, and the Liang founder also commended him.
units.literal: When Jun heard of it, he felt ashamed and fearful and offered thanks; Qing thereby became renowned, and the Liang founder also praised him.

units.zh: 頃入梁，曆給諫、御史中丞、禮部侍郎、知貢舉，咸有能名。
units.en: Under the Liang he served in succession as supervising secretary, censor-in-chief, vice minister of rites, and director of the civil examinations, earning a name for competence at each post.
units.literal: Qing entered Liang and served successively as Supervising Secretary, Censor-in-Chief, Vice Minister of Rites, and Director of the Examinations; in all he had a reputation for ability.

units.zh: 自吏部侍郎拜中書門下平章事，與李琪同輔梁室，事多矛盾。
units.en: Promoted from vice minister of personnel to grand councilor, he served the Liang court alongside Li Qi, and the two often clashed.
units.literal: From Vice Minister of Personnel he was appointed Grand Councilor of the Secretariat and Chancellery; together with Li Qi he assisted the Liang house, and their affairs were often at odds.

units.zh: 莊宗入汴，頃坐貶登州司戶，量移濮州司馬。
units.en: When Emperor Zhuangzong took Bian, Qing was demoted to registrar of Deng Prefecture and transferred by commutation of place to vice prefect of Pu Prefecture.
units.literal: When Zhuangzong entered Bian, Qing was demoted and appointed Registrar of Deng Prefecture, then transferred by degree to Vice Prefect of Pu Prefecture.

units.zh: 數年，遷太子賓客。
units.en: Several years later he was appointed guest of the heir apparent.
units.literal: After several years he was transferred to Guest of the Heir Apparent.

units.zh: 天成初，為禮部尚書、太常卿、太子少保致仕。
units.en: Early in the Tiancheng era he became minister of rites and director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, then retired as junior guardian of the heir apparent.
units.literal: At the beginning of Tiancheng he served as Minister of Rites, Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, and Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent in retirement.

units.zh: 卒時年六十九。
units.en: He died at the age of sixty-nine.
units.literal: When he died he was sixty-nine years old.

units.zh: 輟朝一日，贈太子少師。
units.en: The court suspended audiences for one day, and he was posthumously granted the title junior tutor of the heir apparent.
units.literal: Court was suspended for one day, and he was posthumously granted Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent.

units.zh: 史臣曰：夫相輔之才，從古難得，蓋文學政事，履行謀猷，不可缺一故也。
units.en: The historiographer remarks: Men fit to serve as chief ministers have always been rare, because literary learning, administrative skill, personal conduct, and strategic counsel are alike indispensable.
units.literal: The historiographer states: Talent for assisting in government has from antiquity been hard to obtain, for literary learning and administrative affairs, conduct and stratagems, cannot lack any one of them.

units.zh: 如數君子者，皆互有所長，亦近代之良相也。
units.en: The gentlemen treated here each excelled in different respects and may be counted among the worthy ministers of recent times.
units.literal: Men such as these several gentlemen each had strengths in turn and were also fine ministers of recent times.

units.zh: 如齊公之明節，李琪之文章，足以圭表搢紳，笙簧典誥，陟之廊廟，宜無愧焉！
units.en: The Duke of Qi's luminous integrity and Li Qi's literary mastery were enough to set a standard for the gentry and to lend grace to state documents; when such men entered the highest councils of government, they had nothing to be ashamed of!
units.literal: Such as Duke Qi's bright integrity and Li Qi's literary compositions—sufficient to be a jade measure for the gentry and to sound through canonical edicts—when raised to the hall of state, they should have no shame!

units.zh: 戊午，以前太子少師薛廷珪為檢校戶部尚書、太子少師致仕；
units.en: On wuwu Xue Tinggui was made acting revenue minister and retired Grand Mentor;
units.literal: On wuwu former Grand Mentor of the Heir Xue Tinggui was made acting Minister of Revenue and Grand Mentor emeritus;

units.zh: 又害太子詹事馬道殷、將作監許岩士，貶宰相朱樸，皆昭宗寵昵者也。
units.en: He also killed Ma Daoyin and Xu Yanshi and demoted Zhu Pu, all Zhaozong favorites.
units.literal: He also killed Crown Prince Administrator Ma Daoyin and Construction Commissioner Xu Yanshi, and demoted Chief Minister Zhu Pu—all men Zhaozong favored.

units.zh: 以金紫光祿大夫、行尚書吏部侍郎、上柱國、蘭陵縣開國男、食邑三百戶蕭頃為中書門下平章事，仍進封蘭陵縣開國伯，加食邑四百戶。
units.en: Xiao Qing, acting Vice Minister of Personnel and Baron of Lanling, was made Grand Counselor and advanced to Earl of Lanling with four hundred added households.
units.literal: Purple-Gold Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, acting Vice Minister of Personnel, Pillar of State, Baron of Lanling with three hundred households Xiao Qing was made Grand Counselor, still advanced to Earl of Lanling with four hundred added households.

units.zh: 初，學士竇夢征草錢鏐麻，貶蓬萊尉，帝召專入翰林，遣崇政使李振問宰相云：「專是宰臣蕭頃女婿，令中書商量可否？」
units.en: Earlier, Dou Mengzheng had drafted Qian Liu's edict and was banished to Penglai; the Emperor now summoned Zhuan to the Hanlin and sent Li Zhen to ask: "Zhuan is Xiao Qing's son-in-law—should the Secretariat weigh this?"
units.literal: Earlier, academician Dou Mengzheng had drafted Qian Liu's appointment edict and was demoted to subprefect of Penglai; the Emperor summoned Zhuan into the Hanlin and sent Chongzheng commissioner Li Zhen to ask the chancellors: "Zhuan is Chancellor Xiao Qing's son-in-law—should the Secretariat discuss whether this is permissible?"

units.zh: 夏四月丁未，以宣徽院使、右衛上將軍趙縠權知青州軍州事，以宣徽院副使韋堅權知本院事。
units.en: On dingwei in the fourth month of summer, Zhao Gu, Xuanhui Court commissioner and Right Guard senior general, was made acting commissioner for Qingzhou's military and prefectural affairs; Xuanhui Court deputy commissioner Wei Jian was made acting head of that court.
units.literal: On dingwei in the fourth month of summer, Xuanhui Court commissioner and Right Guard senior general Zhao Gu was made acting Qing prefect military and prefectural commissioner; Xuanhui Court deputy commissioner Wei Jian was made acting head of that court.

units.zh: 甲寅，以刑部郎中、充史館修撰竇專為翰林學士。
units.en: On jiayin, Dou Zhuan, Ministry of Punishments director and History Office compiler, entered the Hanlin Academy.
units.literal: On jiayin, Ministry of Punishments bureau director and History Office compiler Dou Zhuan was made Hanlin academician.

units.zh: 時監軍使劉重楚，季述兄也，舊相張浚，寓於河南緱氏，亦來謂太祖曰：「同中官則事易濟，且得所欲。」
units.en: Military inspector Liu Chongchu, Jishu's elder brother, and former chancellor Zhang Jun lodging at Gou in Henan also urged the Founder: "Side with the eunuchs and all goes easily—you get what you want."
units.literal: At that time military inspector Liu Chongchu, Jishu's elder brother, and former chief minister Zhang Jun lodging at Gou in Henan, also came to tell the Founder: "Join the inner attendants and affairs go easily, and you get what you want."

units.zh: 太祖英悟，忽厲色曰：「張公勸我同敕使，欲傾附自求宰相耶！」
units.en: The Founder was sharp-witted; suddenly he said sternly: "Lord Zhang wants me to join the edict commissioners—are you angling to topple me and buy the chancellorship!"
units.literal: The Founder was keen-witted; suddenly with stern countenance he said: "Lord Zhang urges me to join the edict commissioners—do you wish to topple and attach yourself to seek the chancellorship!"

units.zh: 初，盧程寄褐遊燕，與同志二人謁焉。
units.en: Early on Lu Cheng, traveling in Yan in plain robes, visited him with two companions.
units.literal: Early on Lu Cheng, wearing plain robes while traveling in Yan, visited him with two like-minded companions.

units.zh: 又二十年，盧程登庸於鄴下。
units.en: Twenty years on, Lu Cheng indeed reached high office at Yedu.
units.literal: Twenty years later Lu Cheng rose to high office at Yedu.

units.zh: 元豹謂鄉人張殷袞曰：「適二君子，明年花發，俱為故人。
units.en: Yuanbao told his townsman Zhang Yingun, "Those two visitors—when the flowers bloom next year they will both be dead.
units.literal: Yuanbao said to his townsman Zhang Yingun: "Those two gentlemen just now—when the flowers bloom next year they will both be departed friends.

units.zh: 初，貞明中，史臣李琪、張袞、郤殷象、馮錫嘉奉詔修撰《太祖實錄》三十卷，敘述非工，事多漏略。
units.en: Early in Zhenming, Li Qi, Zhang Gun, Xi Yinxiang, and Feng Xijia were ordered to compile thirty scrolls of the 《Veritable Records of the Founding Emperor》; the narrative was poor and much was left out.
units.literal: At the start, in Zhenming, historians Li Qi, Zhang Gun, Xi Yinxiang, and Feng Xijia received edict to compile the 《Veritable Records of the Founding Emperor》 thirty scrolls; the narration was unskilled and affairs were much omitted.

units.zh: 及劉鄩失河朔，安彥之喪楊劉，翔奏曰：「國家連年遣將出征，封疆日削，不獨兵驕將怯，亦製置未得其術。
units.en: After Liu Xun lost Hebei and An Yanzhi lost Yangliu, Xiang memorialized: "Year after year we send armies abroad while our borders shrink—not only are the troops arrogant and the generals timid; our strategy is wrong as well.
units.literal: When Liu Xun lost Hebei, and An Yanzhi lost Yangliu, Xiang memorialized saying: "The state year after year sends generals on campaign; the borders daily shrink—not only are troops arrogant and generals timid; disposition too has not obtained its method.

units.zh: 御史大夫薛貽矩為押金寶使，尚書左丞趙光逢副之。
units.en: Censor-in-Chief Xue Yiju was made chief custodian of the gold regalia, with Left Assistant Minister Zhao Guangfeng as deputy.
units.literal: Censor-in-Chief Xue Yiju was made chief custodian of the gold regalia, with Left Assistant Minister of the Secretariat Zhao Guangfeng as deputy.

units.zh: 張文蔚、蘇循奉冊升殿進讀，楊涉、張策、薛貽矩、趙光逢以次奉寶升殿，讀已，降，帥百官舞蹈稱駕。
units.en: Zhang Wenwei and Su Xun presented and read the register; Yang She, Zhang Ce, Xue Yiju, and Zhao Guangfeng presented the seals in turn; then they led the court in the bowing dance and acclamation.
units.literal: Zhang Wenwei and Su Xun bore the register up the hall and read it; Yang She, Zhang Ce, Xue Yiju, and Zhao Guangfeng in turn bore the seals up the hall; when the reading was done they descended and led the hundred officials in ritual dance and acclamation.

units.zh: 《通鑒》：甲辰，唐昭宣帝降御劄禪位於梁。
units.en: The 《Zizhi Tongjian》 notes: On jiachen Emperor Zhaoxuan of Tang issued an imperial decree abdicating to Liang.
units.literal: The 《Zizhi Tongjian》 says: On jiachen, Tang's Emperor Zhaoxuan issued an imperial decree abdicating the throne to Liang.

units.zh: 以禮部尚書王正言為戶部尚書，以御史中丞崔協為禮部尚書，以刑部侍郎、史館修撰、判館事崔居儉為御史中丞，以尚書左丞歸靄為刑部侍郎。
units.en: Wang Zhengyan, Minister of Rites, was made Minister of Revenue; Cui Xie, censor-in-chief, was made Minister of Rites; Cui Jujian, Vice Minister of Punishments, History Office compiler, and acting institute director, was made censor-in-chief; and Gui Ai, Left Assistant Director of the Department of State Affairs, was made Vice Minister of Punishments.
units.literal: Minister of Rites Wang Zhengyan was made Minister of Revenue; censor-in-chief Cui Xie was made Minister of Rites; Punishments vice minister, History Office compiler, and acting institute director Cui Jujian was made censor-in-chief; Left Assistant Director of the Department of State Affairs Gui Ai was made Punishments vice minister.

units.zh: 高劭，字子將，淮南節度使駢之從子也。
units.en: Gao Shao, who styled himself Zijiang, was a cousin of the Huainan commissioner Gao Pian.
units.literal: Gao Shao, styled Zijiang, was the younger cousin of Huainan military commissioner Gao Pian.

units.zh: 俄而州陷於蔡，劭為賊所得，使人守之，戒四門曰：「無出高大夫。」
units.en: Soon Cai rebels took the city; they seized Shao and posted guards with orders at every gate: "Let no one let Lord Gao out."
units.literal: Soon the prefecture fell to Cai; Shao was taken by bandits; they sent men to guard him and warned the four gates: "Do not let High Excellency out."

units.zh: 唐僖宗避敵在蜀，駢鎮淮南為都統，兼諸道鹽鐵使，兵賦在己，朝廷優假之，以故劭幸而早官，年十四遙領華州刺史。
units.en: While Xizong sheltered in Shu, Pian ruled Huainan as supreme commander and salt-and-iron commissioner with troops and taxes in his fist; the court indulged him, and Shao at fourteen was given distant command as prefect of Hua.
units.literal: Tang Emperor Xizong avoided the enemy in Shu; Pian held Huainan as supreme commander and concurrently salt and iron commissioner for all circuits, troops and levies in his own hands—the court treated him generously; thus Shao by fortune received early office, at age fourteen distantly holding Hua Prefecture.

units.zh: 太祖以客禮遇之，尋表為亳州團練副使，知州事。
units.en: The Founder received him as an honored guest and soon made him vice-regimental commissioner at Bozhou with charge of the prefecture.
units.literal: The Founder treated him with guest rites; soon memorialized him as Bozhou regimental vice-commissioner and acting prefectural affairs.

units.zh: 光啟中，以駢命遏晉公王鐸於鄭。
units.en: Midway through Guangqi he blocked Wang Duo, Duke of Jin, at Zheng on Pian's order.
units.literal: Mid Guangqi, on Pian's order he blocked the Duke of Jin Wang Duo at Zheng.

units.zh: 行至高陵，為盜所害。
units.en: on the road at Gaoling bandits killed him.
units.literal: traveling, reaching Gaoling, he was harmed by bandits.

units.zh: 劭伺守者稍惰，佯為乞食者，過危垣，取殍者衣，坌身易服，得他兒抱之行，出東郊門。
units.en: When the guards slackened he played a beggar, crept past a broken wall, dressed in a dead man's rags, took up another child as if his own, and walked out the eastern gate.
units.literal: Shao watched until guards slackened slightly, pretended to be a beggar-for-food, passed a perilous wall, took a corpse's clothes, covered his body and changed dress, got another child to carry and walked, exiting the eastern suburb gate.

units.zh: 人以為丐者，不之止。
units.en: Passers took him for a beggar and let him go.
units.literal: People took him for a beggar and did not stop him.

units.zh: 及稍遠，棄所抱兒，疾趨至中牟，遂達於汴。
units.en: Once he was clear of the city he abandoned the child, ran to Zhongmu, and reached Bian.
units.literal: When somewhat far, he abandoned the child he carried, hastened swiftly to Zhongmu, and at last reached Bian.

units.zh: 唐昭宗之鳳翔，太祖迎奉未出，劭有疑謀，遂令赴華州，詣丞相府以議其事；
units.en: When Zhaozong fled to Fengxiang and the Founder had not yet marched to receive him, Shao's plotting aroused suspicion; he was sent to Hua to consult the chief minister's office—
units.literal: Tang Emperor Zhaozong went to Fengxiang; the Founder had not yet gone out to welcome him; Shao had doubtful schemes; he was then ordered to go to Hua Prefecture, to approach the chief minister's office to deliberate the affair;

units.zh: 丙子，樞密使李紹宏與宰相豆盧革、韋說會於中興殿之廊下，商議軍機，因奏：「魏王西征兵士將至，車駕且宜控汜水，以俟魏王。」
units.en: On bingzi Li Shaohong met Dou Luge and Wei Shuo in the Zhongxing corridor and said, "Jiji's western troops are near—the carriage should hold at Sishui to await him."
units.literal: On bingzi Privy Council commissioner Li Shaohong met with chancellors Dou Luge and Wei Shuo in the corridor below the Zhongxing Hall and discussed military affairs; they therefore memorialized, "Prince of Wei Jiji's western campaign soldiers are about to arrive—the imperial carriage should for the moment hold Sishui to await the Prince of Wei."

units.zh: 以吏部侍郎崔協為御史中丞。
units.en: Cui Xie of Personnel became censor-in-chief.
units.literal: Vice Minister of Personnel Cui Xie was made Censor-in-chief.
